title: Prefix Sum Patterns
subtitle: Complete OA Reference — Medium to Hard · Brute Force to Optimal · Complexity · Dry Runs · LeetCode Problems
author: Mayank Verma · IIIT Kottayam
overview:
**Prefix sum converts an expensive range operation into a single O(1) lookup.** Build once in O(n), answer any range query in O(1). All 6 variations share this idea — only the *algebra* changes.

**Core formula:** `sum(l, r) = prefix[r+1] - prefix[l]` (0-padded sentinel at index 0)

structureSignals: Multiple range queries on a *static* (immutable) array ⇒ build prefix array once
Count / find subarrays satisfying some aggregate property ⇒ prefix + HashMap
Bulk range additions, read final values ⇒ difference array

variationsSummary.keyIdea: Immutable array, multiple range sum queries
Count/find subarrays with sum = k; handles negatives

decisionGuide: **Range SUM query, no updates, 1D array?** → Variation 1 (Basic 1-D)
**Range SUM query, no updates, 2D matrix?** → Variation 3 (2-D Prefix Sum)
**Count / find subarrays with sum = k?** → Variation 2 (HashMap template)
**Range ADD updates, read final values?** → Variation 4 (Difference Array)
**Sum divisible by k / pairs with equal remainder?** → Variation 5 (Prefix Mod k)
**XOR of subarray / count subarrays with XOR = k?** → Variation 6 (Prefix XOR)
**2D matrix + count submatrices with sum = k?** → Variation 3 extended with Variation 2 (fix 2 rows)
**Array has negatives, need subarray sum = k?** → Variation 2 (sliding window won't work)

universalTemplate.label: One HashMap template for Variations 2, 5, and 6

commonMistakes: **Forgetting `map.put(0,1)` or `map.put(0,-1)`:** Misses subarrays / subarrays of length >= 2 starting at index 0.
**Querying after inserting:** Always look up the map first, then insert the current prefix — otherwise zero-length subarrays are double-counted.
**Negative modulo in Java:** `(-7)%5 = -2`. Use `((x % k) + k) % k` always.
**Off-by-one:** `sum(l,r) = P[r+1]-P[l]`, not `P[r]-P[l-1]`. Choose one convention and be consistent throughout.
**Integer overflow:** Use `long[]` when values are up to 10^9 and n is up to 10^5 — their product overflows `int`.

variations.name: Basic 1-D Prefix Sum
variations.coreIdea: Given array [a0, a1, ..., a(n-1)], build prefix array P of size n+1 where `P[0] = 0`, `P[i] = P[i-1] + a[i-1]`, and `rangeSum(l,r) = P[r+1] - P[l]`.

boxes.body: We precompute all "running totals" from index 0. Then any subarray sum [l..r] is just the difference of two running totals: we subtract everything *before* l from everything *up to* r. The overlapping prefix [0..l-1] cancels out perfectly.

items: Without prefix sum: answering q range-sum queries costs O(n*q) — untenable for n, q ~ 10^5.
With prefix sum: O(n) one-time build makes every subsequent query O(1).
The 0-padded sentinel at `P[0]` eliminates special-case code for subarrays starting at index 0.
Prefix sum assumes the array is **immutable** — updates require a different structure (Fenwick Tree / Segment Tree).
**0-pad sentinel:** Always make prefix of size n+1 with `P[0]=0` — eliminates boundary checks.
**Off-by-one guard:** `sum(l,r) = P[r+1] - P[l]` — right index is inclusive, add 1 on the right only.
**Long overflow:** Use `long[]` if values can reach 10^9 with n up to 10^5.
**Prefix product:** Same idea with multiplication — useful in "product except self" problems.
**Suffix arrays:** Build from right to left: `S[i] = S[i+1] + a[i]` — pair with prefix for O(1) "product except self".

boxes.title: Dry Run — nums = [3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9], query(2, 4)

variations.name: Prefix Sum + HashMap (Subarray Sum = K)
variations.coreIdea: If `P[j] - P[i] = k`, then subarray [i..j-1] sums to k. Rearranging: we need `P[i] = P[j] - k` to exist in the map *before* reaching j. So `count += map.getOrDefault(P[j] - k, 0)`.

boxes.body: Instead of checking all pairs (i, j) in O(n^2), we flip the question: "how many earlier prefix sums equal P[j] - k?" We look this up in O(1) using a frequency HashMap. The key insight is that we are counting valid *left endpoints* for each right endpoint j as we sweep left-to-right.

items: Works with **negative numbers and zeros** — unlike the sliding window technique, which requires non-negative values.
Initializing `map.put(0, 1)` accounts for subarrays that start at index 0 (empty prefix has value 0 and has been "seen" once before we start).
We must **query before inserting** — if we insert first, we may use the current index as its own left endpoint, creating a zero-length subarray.
For the "longest subarray" variant, store the *first occurrence index* instead of frequency, and use `putIfAbsent`.
**Always init `map.put(0,1)`** — without it, subarrays starting at index 0 are missed.
**Insert AFTER query** — inserting before double-counts zero-length subarrays.
**Longest subarray variant:** Use `map.putIfAbsent(prefixSum, i)` and compute `maxLen = i - map.get(prefixSum - k)`.
**Existence only:** If you only need to know *whether* a subarray with sum k exists, replace `Map` with `Set` and `set.contains(prefixSum - k)`.
**"Exactly k" via "at most k":** For non-negative arrays, f(exactly k) = f(at most k) - f(at most k-1) combined with sliding window.

variations.name: 2-D Prefix Sum
variations.coreIdea: For matrix mat[m][n], build P[m+1][n+1] with a 0-border: `P[i][j] = mat[i-1][j-1] + P[i-1][j] + P[i][j-1] - P[i-1][j-1]`. Rectangle query (r1,c1) → (r2,c2): `sum = P[r2+1][c2+1] - P[r1][c2+1] - P[r2+1][c1] + P[r1][c1]`.

boxes.body: Think of `P[i][j]` as the area of a rectangle from the top-left corner (0,0) to (i-1, j-1). To get any sub-rectangle, we take the big rectangle, subtract the two over-counted strips (above and to the left), then add back the corner that was double-subtracted. A = big rect up to (r2,c2), B = strip above, C = strip left, D = corner (double-subtracted). **Answer = A - B - C + D**

items: The (m+1)x(n+1) zero-border eliminates all edge/corner special cases.
Build is O(mn); every subsequent query is O(1) — essential when Q >> 1.
For "count submatrices with sum = target": fix two rows, reduce to 1-D Variation 2 on column sums.
"Max sum sub-rectangle <= k": fix rows, then use a sorted set (TreeSet) for binary search on column prefix sums.

variations.name: Difference Array (Range Updates)
variations.coreIdea: When you need to **add v to every element in [l, r]** for q updates, naive is O(n) per update. Instead, record only the boundary changes — `diff[l] += v`, `diff[r+1] -= v` — then reconstruct with a prefix sum at the end.

boxes.body: A range update [l, r] += v affects all elements in [l, r] equally. Instead of writing v to every cell (expensive), we mark "v starts flowing at l" and "v stops flowing after r". When we finally take the prefix sum of the diff array, the running total automatically propagates v through every index from l to r — and cancels back to 0 at r+1.

items: This is the **inverse** of prefix sum: prefix sum answers range queries; difference array enables range updates.
O(1) per update, O(n) to reconstruct at the end — total O(n + q).
Cannot answer *point queries mid-update* — reconstruct only after all updates are applied.
Extends to **2D difference arrays** for matrix rectangle updates.
Common OA framing: "passengers board at stop A, exit at stop B" ⇒ `diff[A]++, diff[B+1]--`.
**Size n+1:** Writing to `diff[r+1]` when r = n-1 accesses index n — valid because array is size n+1.
**2-D difference array:** For rectangle update (r1,c1)→(r2,c2) by v: apply +v at (r1,c1), -v at (r1,c2+1), -v at (r2+1,c1), +v at (r2+1,c2+1). Then 2D prefix sum reconstructs.
**Not for mid-update point queries** — reconstruct only after all updates are applied.
**Event simulation:** Any problem where events "start" and "end" at known positions maps cleanly onto a difference array.

variations.name: Prefix Sum Mod k (Divisibility)
variations.coreIdea: **Key theorem:** If `P[i] ≡ P[j] (mod k)` with i < j, then `P[j] - P[i]` is divisible by k, meaning subarray [i..j-1] has sum divisible by k. Count pairs of indices with equal remainder ⇒ use a frequency map of remainders: `count += freq[P[j] mod k]`.

boxes.body: Two prefix sums that share the same remainder modulo k define a subarray whose sum is a multiple of k — because their difference is exactly divisible by k. So we reduce the problem to: "count pairs of equal remainders in the prefix sum sequence". A frequency array of size k is sufficient since there are only k possible remainders.

items: Space is O(k), not O(n), since there are only k possible remainders [0, k-1].
If remainder r appears f times, it contributes C(f,2) = f(f-1)/2 valid pairs.
**Java gotcha:** `-7 % 5 = -2` in Java. Always normalize: `((x % k) + k) % k`.
Initializing `freq[0] = 1` handles subarrays starting at index 0 that are themselves divisible by k.

boxes.title: Critical Gotcha — Negative Modulo in Java / C++
boxes.body: In Java: `-7 % 5 = -2` (NOT 3). In C++: also implementation-defined for negatives pre-C++11. Always normalize: `rem = ((prefixSum % k) + k) % k`. This ensures the remainder is always in [0, k-1].

items: init: prefixSum = 0, rem = 0, freq = {0:1}, count = 0
i=0, num=4: prefixSum=4, rem=4, count=0, freq={0:1,4:1}
i=1, num=5: prefixSum=9, rem=4, count += 1 → 1, freq={0:1,4:2}
i=2, num=0: prefixSum=9, rem=4, count += 2 → 3, freq={0:1,4:3}
i=3, num=-2: prefixSum=7, rem=2, count=3
i=4, num=-3: prefixSum=4, rem=4, count += 3 → 6, freq={...,4:4}
i=5, num=1: prefixSum=5, rem=0, count += 1 → 7
**Answer: 7** subarrays with sum divisible by 5.

variations.name: Prefix XOR
variations.coreIdea: XOR properties: x^x = 0, x^0 = x, commutative and associative. Define `X[i] = a[0] ^ a[1] ^ ... ^ a[i-1]`, with `X[0] = 0`. Then `rangeXOR(l, r) = X[r+1] ^ X[l]`, because the overlapping prefix cancels. For subarray XOR = k: we need `X[i] = X[j] ^ k`, so use a HashMap.

boxes.body: XOR prefix arrays work identically to sum prefix arrays, but the algebra changes: subtraction becomes XOR. When two prefix XOR values are XOR-ed together, all bits in the overlapping prefix cancel (x^x = 0), leaving only the XOR of the non-overlapping part. To find a prefix that XOR-combined with the current gives k, look up `currentXOR ^ k` in the HashMap.

items: XOR is its own inverse: no "negative" issue unlike modulo.
The lookup key changes: sum version checks `prefixSum - k`; XOR version checks `xorSum ^ k`.
**Count Triplets trick:** If XOR of [i..j] is 0, then for any split point between i and j, both halves have equal XOR — yields j - i valid triplets.
**Max XOR subarray:** Use prefix XOR + Trie, greedily picking the opposite bit at each level — O(32n).
**Lookup difference:** Sum version checks `prefixSum - k`; XOR version checks `xorSum ^ k`. Same structure, different operator.
**XOR self-cancellation:** a^a = 0 — this is what makes range queries work.
**Trie for max XOR:** For "max XOR of any subarray/pair", insert prefix XOR values in a Trie and greedily pick the opposite bit at each of the 31 levels.
**Count Triplets shortcut:** If XOR of [i..j] is 0, then any split k between gives equal halves — that's j - i valid triplets.
**No negative normalization needed:** XOR is always non-negative and self-inverse — no modulo headaches.
